ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mirъ (“peace; world”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *meiˀrás (“peace”), from Proto-Indo-European *mey(H)-ró-s. Russian uses the regular dual meaning of "peace" and "world" that was usual in Old Slavic; this Slavic feature considered unique. The peace/world ambiguity is saved in some other Slavic languages, such as Bulgarian, but with the sense of "world" it remains there as a dated or poetic term. The pre-1918 orthography had an orthographical distinction of the two identically pronounced words to avoid confusion (see Alternative forms).
